the training of deep neural nets with SGD is a complex interplay between the learning rate, batch-size, and the curvature of the training loss surface.

the dynamics of the SGD in the subspace corresponding to the sharpest directions in the loss landscape influence the regions that it steers to (larger learning rate or smaller batches result in wider regions), the overall training dynamics and the generalization performance of the final model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the training dynamics in the sharpest directions of the loss surface is important for training deep neural networks.
SGD is a complex process that cannot be understood by studying the loss surface alone, and that the loss surface is only one of the many factors that influence the training dynamics.
SGD dynamics in the sharpest directions can be used to improve the training of deep neural nets, by either avoiding sharp regions or by steering SGD to sharper regions.
